title: Choose the visual world for xd
question: The roll assigned Card Catalog. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Card Catalog
options.lineage: library card catalogs: oak drawers, brass label frames, ruled index cards, metal signal tabs
options.thesis: Projects are drawers, sessions are index cards, and a coloured signal tab on each card says what its agent is doing.
materials: card stock with one red ruled header line
options.viewport: One sidebar of project drawers; the open drawer shows its session cards with signal tabs; the chat fills the centre; changes/terminal/browser dock right.
options.risk: Can tip into warm-brown nostalgia if the wood and brass are used as texture instead of as two flat tones.

raised.raise: State reads in the tab's form as well as its hue: solid for running, outlined for queued, struck through for failed, so it survives grayscale.
One ink is reserved: the amber tab appears only when an agent is waiting on you (an approval or a question).
Nothing disappears, it gets stamped: a stopped or failed session stays in its drawer with its stamp until you file it away.
The open drawer lifts; the other drawers compress to one line each, showing only their tabs.
Every card row keeps one fixed height and baseline across the sidebar and panes.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: Swiss and German station departure boards
options.thesis: Each project is a platform and each session a departure, with a status column that changes in yellow like a platform change.
options.viewport: A board-like session table per project, status column on the right, the chat to its right; panes dock beside it.
options.risk: Transit metaphors are common for operations tools, and the navy ground sits close to the dark mode you just rejected.

options.label: Developer Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels separated by hairline seams, with syntax-derived colours used only for state.
options.viewport: Persistent tiled panels: sessions, chat, changes; navigation swaps panel contents, never the layout.
options.case: Holds product clarity, since it reads instantly as a dev tool, but loses audience identification: it is close to the graphite-plus-one-accent look you just rejected.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of anonymity; with the name covered it could be any editor.

options.label: Emission-line Rail
options.thesis: State carried by line height, dash and doubling on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: Destinations as ticks on one rail.
options.risk: Its rail navigation would replace standard navigation.
options.case: Loses both axes: a spectrogram is far from the user's world, and rail navigation hides the project-then-session hierarchy.
options.kept: State in form as well as hue.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Coupons that stamp their state instead of vanishing.
options.risk: A linear coupon flow fights many parallel sessions.
options.case: Loses both axes: sessions run in parallel, not as a sequence of legs.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: The focused row lifts while the rest dims.
options.case: Loses both axes: sessions have no artwork, and tiles cut density.
options.kept: The open drawer lifts; the others compress.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed colour language, with one ink reserved for the active course.
options.viewport: A map with a purple course.
options.risk: Map metaphors don't fit a session list.
options.case: Loses both axes: there is no terrain in this product.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Fixed-scale plates on one shared baseline.
options.case: Loses both axes: an editorial world for a working tool.
options.kept: One fixed row height and baseline everywhere.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral-gray editor shell with one blue accent, as in Zed, VS Code or Cursor, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Activity bar, explorer tree, editor tabs, side panels, status bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every editor by design.
